messages:
maya: fyi seeing a correctness hole in streaming read-paths when a prefix gets demoted while a long-lived session is in-flight. some sessions return values from the demoted slab after we already told the tenant the prefix was 'not resident'.
orion: can you paste the minimal repro logs? curious if it's a visibility window or ordering bug.
maya: log snippet —
```
[2100151229] session=zz-stream-42 serve:k=prefix:abcd state=served_from_cache slab=3 gen=17
[2100151230] controller:demote prefix=abcd slab=3 gen=18 -> mark_nonresident
[2100151231] session=zz-stream-42 serve:k=prefix:abcd state=served_from_cache slab=3 gen=17
[2100151232] tenant-observer: saw_nonresident prefix=abcd at t=2100151230
```
so the controller marks non-resident at gen=18 but the session still uses gen=17 cache entries. we end up telling the upper layer two conflicting things in a short window.
devin: hunch: session had no resident-check fastpath so it just read slab pointer and served. we only remove slab pointer asynchronously. two problems: (1) we don't tag served entries with the latest residency epoch, (2) we don't surface a 'served-but-stale' signal to the caller.
sasha: +1. also need a metric for "served-after-demote". without it we'll regress silently. propose a counter per-prefix and an e2e latency spike tag.
orion: design options:
- atomic demote: ensure demote swings both controller index and per-slab serve-flag under the same lock (fast but may block serving threads)
- optimistic tag: attach a small residency_epoch to cache handles; sessions check epoch before final write to downstream and retry on mismatch (non-blocking)
- session-cohort lease: give in-flight sessions a short lease that keeps current entries resident until they finish (complex for eviction pressure)
what do we prefer?
tj: leaning toward optimistic tag. minimal runtime change: when we hand out a handle include epoch=controller.current_epoch. demote bumps epoch. serving path compares handle. if mismatch, switch to resolve path (fetch fresh or fallback). avoids global locks.
maya: optimistic tag sounds good, but we need to define failure mode: do we block the session's token emit, return a special status to runtime to fetch from remote, or force short-circuit fallback model? we must keep latency SLOs.
devin: implementation sketch:
1) struct Handle { slab_id, ptr, epoch }
2) serve(handle) { if (handle.epoch < controller.epoch_for(prefix)) { metrics.inc("served_post_epoch"); goto resolve; } return use(ptr); }
3) resolve: try atomic re-resolve prefix residency (cheap sync path) else fall back to remote fetch.
this keeps most fast-paths lock-free.
sasha: add metric tags: prefix, tenant, callsite. and an alert rule when served_post_epoch > 0.1% of requests for a minute. also record p90 latency of resolve path.
orion: edge case: two quick demotes could cause repeated resolve churn. maybe we add a per-session backoff to avoid thundering. or combine with a short-lived session pin (lease) for first resolve retry.
tj: agree on per-session backoff of 50-200ms jittered. that plus optimistic tag should prevent storms.
maya: ok action items: (1) devin to prototype handle+epoch and add served_post_epoch metric (2) sasha to add grafana panel + alert (3) orion to write short RFC for epoch semantics and backoff strategy (4) tj to add unit tests for resolve path and a small perf run.
deploy-bot: CI: test-suite started for branch prefix-epoch-proto (9 jobs). will post results in thread. :robot_face:
maya: thanks — will wait for CI and then we can try a canary on dedicated pool with long-lived-stream test harness.
